title: Mixed Flow Pump
model_title: Mixed Flow Pump (Vertical Wet-Pit, Single Stage)

introduction.definition: A mixed flow pump has impellers whose flow leaves at an angle between radial and axial, combining centrifugal and lift forces. It sits between radial and axial pumps in specific speed: higher flow than a radial pump and more head than an axial pump.
key_points: Non-overloading or slightly rising power curve depending on design

classification.configuration: Vertical wet pit, single stage, line-shaft

introduction.summary: A mixed-flow pump adds energy partly by centrifugal action and partly by the lift of its blades: liquid leaves the impeller diagonally, between the radial direction of a centrifugal pump and the axial direction of a propeller pump. This suits large flows at moderate heads (specific speed roughly between radial and axial machines). In the vertical wet-pit form shown, the bowl hangs in the intake sump and a discharge elbow above the floor turns the flow into the outlet pipe.

what_to_look_for: Water enters through the suction bell.
The mixed-flow impeller discharges diagonally, adding both centrifugal and lift energy.
The diffuser bowl removes swirl and converts velocity to pressure.

steps.text: Water enters through the suction bell.
The mixed-flow impeller discharges diagonally, adding both centrifugal and lift energy.
The diffuser bowl removes swirl and converts velocity to pressure.
The column and elbow lead the water to discharge.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Moderately steep head curve; power approximately flat across the range for many designs.

parts.function: Diffuser casing for one stage: converts swirl leaving the impeller into pressure and guides flow to the next impeller.

parts.name: Taper Lock Collet – Pump 1

parts.name: Suction Bell

parts.name: Suction Bell Bearing

video_tutorials.title: Mixed Flow Pump — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Mixed Flow Pump.
A mixed flow pump has impellers whose flow leaves at an angle between radial and axial, combining centrifugal and lift forces.
It sits between radial and axial pumps in specific speed: higher flow than a radial pump and more head than an axial pump.
Typical applications include irrigation and drainage; cooling-water intakes; municipal raw-water and storm water; flood control.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Discharge Case (Top Bowl), Bowl – Pump 1, Bowl Wear Ring – Pump 1, Impeller – Pump 1.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Mixed Flow Pump works.
Water enters through the suction bell.
The mixed-flow impeller discharges diagonally, adding both centrifugal and lift energy.
The diffuser bowl removes swirl and converts velocity to pressure.
The column and elbow lead the water to discharge.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Mixed Flow Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Mixed Flow Pump.
Monitor vibration and thrust-bearing temperature.
Check impeller clearance.
Inspect impeller and bowl.
Watch for vortex / air entrainment: noise, falling flow. Common cause: low submergence.
Watch for wear: lower performance. Common cause: silt.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
